paper_sections.title: Brain Reactivity to Smoking Cues Prior to Smoking Cessation Predicts Ability to Maintain Tobacco Abstinence
Region-of-Interest (ROI) Analyses: Relation to Smoking Cessation Outcome and Emotional Stroop Performance
Correlations Between FMRI and Emotional Stroop Data

description.value: The study examined whether prequit fMRI reactivity to smoking-related images and attentional bias to smoking-related words could identify nicotine-dependent women who would later slip during a smoking cessation attempt.

design.value: Before quitting smoking, 21 nicotine-dependent women underwent fMRI while viewing smoking-related and neutral images and completed an emotional Stroop task. After a quit attempt, participants were grouped according to whether they maintained abstinence or smoked at least one cigarette after attaining abstinence. Prequit fMRI activation, ROI measures, functional connectivity, and emotional Stroop performance were compared between groups and related to cessation outcomes.

description.value: Administered to characterize nicotine dependence.
Smoking-related and neutral words were displayed in colored fonts, and participants reported word color while ignoring word meaning; reaction times and accuracies were recorded.
Expired air carbon monoxide was measured at screening and weekly during cessation follow-up.
Weekly self-report of smoking behavior in the prior 7 days.

description.value: Twenty-one women underwent neuroimaging at McLean Hospital before participating in a smoking cessation clinical trial at Massachusetts General Hospital.

inclusion_criteria.value: met DSM-IV criteria for current nicotine dependence
reported smoking ≥10 cigarettes per day in the previous 6 months
expired air carbon monoxide (CO) >10 ppmv at screening

exclusion_criteria.value: alcohol use disorder in the prior 6 months
lifetime diagnosis of organic mental or psychotic disorders

recruitment_method.value: before participating in a smoking cessation clinical trial at Massachusetts General Hospital

clinical_characteristics.value: Baseline smoking behavior was characterized by pack-years of tobacco smoking, expiratory CO levels, the number of cigarettes smoked the morning before imaging, and FTND scores.

medication_status.value: Smoking was not restricted until shortly before imaging; after prequit imaging, participants received nicotine patch and nicotine polacrilex gum or lozenge during the cessation phase.

description.value: Participants who smoked any cigarettes during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period after at least 24 hours of abstinence; nine subjects slipped while on NRT.

inclusion_criteria.value: smoked any cigarettes during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period following at least 24 hours abstinence

clinical_characteristics.value: Slips took place on average 17.4 days (range: 1–49 days) after established abstinence.

medication_status.value: Slipped while on nicotine replacement therapy.

description.value: Participants who did not smoke during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period after at least 24 hours of abstinence.

inclusion_criteria.value: did not smoke during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period following at least 24 hours abstinence

clinical_characteristics.value: Subjects who self-reported abstinence and had an expired CO <9 ppmv were considered abstinent.

medication_status.value: Did not smoke during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period.

task_description.value: During fMRI, subjects viewed smoking-related or neutral images. Animal images were included to ensure subjects attended to stimuli but were not used in data analyses.

design_type.value: 6 equal-length blocks; each image was presented pseudo-randomly

stimuli.value: 42 smoking-related images of people smoking, hands holding cigarettes, or cigarettes alone; 40 neutral content-matched images with no smoking cues; and 8 animal images.

task_performance_measures.value: response button presses to animal images

task_description.value: After a 96-trial practice block of letter strings, four 33-trial experimental blocks separated by 5-sec breaks were run in the order neutral, smoking, smoking, neutral; analyses were restricted to the first two blocks.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to report word color as quickly and accurately as possible and to ignore word meaning.

stimuli.value: Smoking-related and neutral words, matched for length and use frequency in the English language, displayed in red, green, or blue fonts.

task_name.value: 8-week smoking cessation phase of the clinical trial

task_description.value: All subjects quit smoking during the 8-week smoking cessation phase of the clinical trial. Interventions included a weekly, manualized individual behavioral intervention, nicotine patch, and nicotine polacrilex gum or lozenge as needed.

task_performance_measures.value: weekly self-report of smoking behavior and weekly expired CO measurements

modality.value: multiplanar rapidly acquired gradient-echo structural images

instrument.value: Siemens Trio 3 Tesla scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a circularly polarized head coil

description.value: Multiplanar rapidly acquired gradient-echo structural images were acquired with 128 slices, a 256 × 256 matrix, and a flip angle of 12°.

instrument.value: Siemens Trio 3 Tesla scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a circularly polarized head coil

description.value: Gradient echo echo-planar images were acquired with 30 slices, a 64 × 64 mm matrix, field of view 224, flip angle 75°, 3.5 mm isotropic resolution, and 0 mm gap.

Images were slice-time corrected, motion corrected, spatially smoothed, resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm isotropic voxels, and spatially normalized into Talairach space. A program was used to model out time points exhibiting motion >1.75 mm.

steps.value: spatial smoothing with a 6-mm Gaussian kernel
modeling out time points exhibiting motion >1.75 mm

model_settings.value: Image regressors for smoking, neutral, and animal images and motion confound regressors; square waves defined by the onset–offset of each image presentation were convolved with the hemodynamic response function. Beta maps comparing smoking with neutral images were created for each subject.
Subject beta maps for the smoking image > neutral image contrast were used to compare fMRI activity between slip and abstinent subject groups.

Accuracy and reaction-time scores were analyzed separately, with Group (slip, abstinent) as a between-subject factor, Condition (neutral vs. smoking-related words) as a repeated measure, and FTND scores as covariates.
Relationships between ROI fMRI activation and emotional Stroop task performance were evaluated.
A cross-validation approach with a leave-one-out classification strategy was used; each case was iteratively classified on the basis of all other cases.

Principal-component analysis data reduction was used to load all data into memory; data were concatenated into a matrix; the GIFT minimum description length algorithm determined 25 optimal components; Component Number 2 containing bilateral insula and anterior cingulate was selected.
Each participant's Component Number 2 time course was converted into a Brain Voyager-compatible regressor; the GLM contained the Component Number 2 time course and motion confound regressors.
Emotional Stroop interference effects predicted mean insular and dACC activity after controlling for FTND scores.
Group differences in baseline smoking behavior were assessed with two-sided Student's t tests.

definition.value: smoking-related images versus neutral images, comparing slip and abstinent subject groups

voxelwise_threshold_type.value: individual voxel Type 1 error of p = .01

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-level correction using a Monte Carlo simulation

model_representation_notes.value: A whole-brain fixed-effects GLM included image regressors for smoking, neutral, and animal images and motion confound regressors; subject-level smoking-versus-neutral beta maps were compared using a random-effects analysis.

interpretations.value: Slip subjects had heightened fMRI reactivity to smoking-related images in brain regions implicated in emotion, interoceptive awareness, and motor planning and execution.
